items.claim: The rejected_alternative's claim that Prov.11.30 shares no wording with 11:31 is byte-false, and the row's only Hebrew quotation is unpointed and unlabeled as skeleton tier.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.11.30 and oshb:Prov.11.31 both carry the byte-identical accented word צַ֭דִּיק (righteous); sweep --heb on that exact pointed form hits both verses at byte tier (17 verses book-wide share the identical accented form; skeleton-tier root ~66 verses book-wide). So the rationale's clause 'shares no wording with this verse's a-fortiori repayment argument' is factually wrong, not merely undisclosed -- the shared word should instead have been named and downweighted as ordinary collection-wide vocabulary, the way sibling rows in this cluster (P06-005, P06-007) correctly disclose and downweight their own shared reshaim term. Separately, the row's quoted Hebrew "הן…אף כי" (cited oshb:Prov.11.31) re-collates via collate.py to tier=skeleton, not byte -- it is unpointed (no niqqud/te'amim) and is presented as a plain quotation with no skeleton-tier label; the correct pointed bytes at that position are הֵ֣ן ... אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי. The underlying single_proverb call is still plausible (tsadiq is too common to itself drive a cluster), but the rationale needs correcting, not just re-stating.

items.claim: The two-negator / adversative-waw construction claim is byte-accurate, but the row quotes no Hebrew for a boundary-relevant original-language claim.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.12.3 confirms the claimed structure at byte tier: the A-colon opens לֹא (the ordinary negator), the B-colon opens וְשֹׁ֥רֶשׁ (waw-prefixed), and closes with בַּל before the verb -- bal is genuinely the rarer poetic negative particle next to lo, and the negator swap plus the waw placement are real, not an artifact of the WEB rendering. Defect: no Hebrew is quoted anywhere in the row for this claim, so it cannot itself be re-collated -- a standing-rule gap (book_strategy Section 8: 'Quote the original language for every boundary-relevant original-language claim'; brief item 1: 'A Hebrew claim with no quoted form is insufficient engagement').

items.claim: The divrei header-vs-construct argument is well-grounded against the device inventory, but the row fails to disclose that its own headword reshaim recurs in both immediate neighbors, breaking cross-seam disclosure symmetry.
items.evidence: Byte tier: the pointed form רְשָׁעִ֣ים in Prov.12.6 is identical to the form in Prov.12.5 and Prov.12.7 (sweep --heb on that exact pointed token hits 16 verses book-wide at byte tier, including Prov.12.5, Prov.12.6, Prov.12.7 consecutively). P06-005 and P06-007 both name this 3-verse chain explicitly and correctly downweight it as ordinary collection-wide vocabulary rather than a driver -- but P06-006's own rationale and rejected_alternative never mention that this verse's own opening noun participates in the same chain. That is an asymmetric disclosure gap under the TOOLKIT's CROSS-SEAM COHESION rule ('a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against the row unless disclosed') and the campaign's SYMMETRY-completion rule. The divrei argument itself is sound against prov_device_inventory.json: Prov.12.6 is one of the 5 divrei_verse_initial verses (12:6, 18:8, 26:22, 30:1, 31:1) but not one of the 2 true collection headers (30:1, 31:1) among 19 total divrei occurrences -- book_strategy Section 2a names 12:6 itself as the worked example of 'verse-initial but not a header,' and the row matches that exactly. No error there, only the missing reshaim disclosure, compounded by no Hebrew quoted for the construct/waw claims either.

items.claim: The B-colon's opening waw is mislabeled: it is a vav-consecutive (wayyiqtol) verb form, not the simple conjunctive waw+noun/participle construction the row's own device_notes equates it with across the cluster, and the row's claim that neighbor 12:14 lacks an adversative waw altogether is byte-false.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.12.13's B-colon opener וַיֵּצֵ֖א carries vav+patach followed by dagesh forte in the yod -- the classic waw-conversive (vayyiqtol) morphology on a finite verb, grammatically distinct from every other 'adversative waw' cited across this cluster's rows: 12:3's וְשֹׁ֥רֶשׁ, 12:6's וּפִ֥י, 12:7's וּבֵ֖ית, 12:15's וְשֹׁמֵ֖עַ, and 12:16's וְכֹסֶ֖ה are all simple conjunctive waw prefixed to a noun or participle (shva- or shuruq-vocalized), with no consecution. Folding both under one 'adversative waw' label in device_notes conflates two different Hebrew constructions behind the same English gloss -- exactly the translation-dependent flattening the OL lens is meant to catch. Separately, oshb:Prov.12.14's B-colon opens וּגְמ֥וּל, a waw-prefixed word (shuruq vav), which directly contradicts the rejected_alternative's claim that 12:14 'lacks an adversative waw altogether' -- a waw is present; at most its force is continuative/synthetic rather than adversative (12:14 is a synonymous, not antithetic, couplet), but 'lacks...altogether' misstates the bytes rather than qualifying the waw's function. No Hebrew is quoted for either claim.
